units.source_text: 山风凛冽，木叶尽脱，四周景象无限凄凉。

en.t: The mountain wind blew bitterly cold, the leaves had all fallen from the trees, and the whole scene around them was endlessly desolate.

units.source_text: 落叶公主受此环境影响，日夜悲叹，泪无干时。

en.t: Princess Ochiba was affected by these surroundings and lamented day and night, with never a moment when her tears were dry.

units.source_text: 她痛恨“生死”也不能“随心意”，便觉人世实在可悲可厌。

en.t: She bitterly resented that even life and death could not follow one's wishes, and she felt that the human world was truly sorrowful and hateful.

units.source_text: 众侍女也都觉得万事可悲，心迷意乱。

en.t: All the waiting women also felt that everything was sorrowful, and their hearts were bewildered and disturbed.

units.source_text: 夕雾大将每日遣使存问，犒赏僧众种种物品，寂寞地诵经念佛的僧众都很喜慰。

en.t: General Yugiri sent messengers every day to ask after them, and he rewarded the monks with various gifts, so the monks who were lonely in their sutra recitation and prayers were greatly comforted.

units.source_text: 又写情深意密的信给公主，向她诉恨，一面又无限殷勤地向她慰问。

en.t: He also wrote deeply affectionate and intimate letters to the princess, expressing his resentment to her while at the same time offering her endlessly attentive consolation.

units.source_text: 但公主看也不看一眼。

en.t: But the princess would not even glance at them.

units.source_text: 她想起那天晚上夕雾的荒唐行为，致使病弱的老夫人以为他们已成事实，因而抱恨死去，成了妨碍往生成佛的罪障，便觉悲愤填胸。

en.t: When she remembered Yugiri's outrageous conduct that night, which had made the frail old lady believe their relationship had become a fact and die in bitterness, creating a sinful obstacle to her rebirth and enlightenment, her heart filled with grief and indignation.

units.source_text: 只要有人约略提及此人，她就痛恨万状，泪下如雨。

en.t: If anyone so much as mentioned him in passing, she was filled with intense hatred and shed tears like rain.

units.source_text: 因此众侍女不敢禀告，徒唤奈何。

en.t: For that reason the waiting women did not dare report anything to her, and could only lament helplessly.

units.source_text: 夕雾连一行回信也收不到，起初以为公主哀思未尽，暂不写信之故，但后来日子太久，只管音信全无。

en.t: Yugiri did not receive even a single line in reply; at first he thought the princess was still overwhelmed by grief and was only temporarily unable to write, but as the days dragged on there was still no word at all.

units.source_text: 他想：“悲哀终有限度，岂可如此忽视我的一片真心！

en.t: He thought, "Even grief has its limits; how can she disregard my sincere heart like this!

units.source_text: 真乃无情过分，太不懂事了。”心中不免怨恨。

en.t: This is far too heartless, and far too lacking in understanding." In his heart, he could not help feeling resentful.

units.source_text: 又想：“如果我信上说的是风花雪月等闲情琐事，固然使她讨厌，

en.t: He also thought, "If my letters were about idle romantic trifles, matters of flowers, wind, snow, and moonlight, then of course they might disgust her,

units.source_text: 但我写的都是同情于她的哀愁和悲伤的慰问之言，她对我应知感谢。

en.t: but everything I wrote was a word of consolation sympathizing with her sorrow and grief, so she ought to feel grateful to me.

units.source_text: 回忆昔年太君逝世，我心悲痛不堪。

en.t: When I remember the year Lady Oigimi died, my heart was unbearably grief-stricken.

units.source_text: 前太政大臣却并不哀伤，认为死别乃人世常事，而只在丧葬仪式上尽其孝道，实甚冷酷无情。

en.t: Yet the former Chancellor did not grieve, treating separation by death as an ordinary thing in this world and merely fulfilling his filial duty through the funeral rites; he was truly cold and heartless.

units.source_text: 六条院父亲大人只是半子，反而诚恳地举办死后种种佛事，使我不胜喜慰——并非为了他是我父亲才这样说。

en.t: My father, Lord Rokujo, was only a son-in-law, yet he sincerely arranged all kinds of Buddhist services after her death, which gave me immense comfort; I do not say this merely because he is my father.

units.source_text: 已故的卫门督也竭尽哀思，因此我从那时候起就特别亲近他。

en.t: The late Captain of the Gate Guards also gave himself fully to mourning her, and from that time on I felt especially close to him.

units.source_text: 柏木为人非常镇静，对世事考虑十分周到，其哀思比常人更为深切，真乃可爱之人。”

en.t: Kashiwagi was an exceptionally composed man, thoughtful in every worldly matter, and his grief was deeper than that of ordinary people; he was truly a lovable person."

units.source_text: 他在寂寞无聊之时，常常如此回想，借以度送日月。

en.t: When he was lonely and bored, he often recalled things in this way, using such thoughts to pass the days and months.
